properties.statement:
Increment 7 of epoch:planned-cognition-plus-memory, part 1. Every tool reflow2 0.95.0 serves (199, from --list-tools) was put in exactly one class.
SOURCES: (1) the recall pilot on 0.93.1, 812 calls in 7 sessions; (2) the increment-3 re-run on 0.94.0, 1,198 calls (six writer sessions, then the answerer), with usage_report's cue block for the writers (683 cues offered, 26 followed within 5 calls, 292 at all); (3) flo2.io's call log 2026-09-24 to 2026-10-30, 22,271 reflow2 tool calls (25,671 connector calls), read-only, counts and order only, no arguments. Times cued adds the pilot's replayed counts to the 0.94.0 ledger's. describe_schema's per-edge-type `hint` text (11 offers each for apply_heal, claim_region, gap_to_prompt, gaps_to_prompts, get_node, open_questions, propagate_from, propose_heal ...) is counted by the ledger as a cue but is reference text, so it is shown separately and not used to class a tool.
METHOD for steps: flo2.io calls grouped by person and design, split at gaps over 3 minutes, refusals dropped, repeats collapsed, reads (get_node, search_design, find_tools, describe_schema, scan_nodes, get_skill, get_instructions, loop_status, graph_report*) skipped; a tool is a step of P when most of its runs have P within two writes, and step-only when it is almost never alone.
CLASSES (precedence D, then B, then E, then A, then C):
A, called: 109. 70 called 10 times or more (get_node 3,883, replace_text 1,376, add_requirement 1,335, add_decision 974, add_change_event 737); 39 called 1 to 9 times, mostly by one person's agents.
B, cued and not followed: 5. detect_gaps cued 119 (loop_hint 97, pilot 22), followed 0; loop_status cued 238, followed within 5 calls 6 and at all 238 (at the end of each round); governed_by cued 31, followed 0; detect_defects cued 26, followed 0; open_questions cued 7, followed 0. Each is called where people and agents needed it on flo2.io (211, 397, 226, 33, 56 calls), so the tool is not what nobody wants: the writer sessions were offered on every write a step they took at the end of a round (loop_status) or never (detect_gaps, governed_by, detect_defects).
C, never cued and never called anywhere: 40. evidence_report, forecast_readiness, frontier, ility_report, granularity_report, consumption_report, surprising_connections, readiness_report, gate_on, set_capability_signature, set_project_mode, set_artifact_intent, set_capability_delivery, alternatives_for, collapse_decision, owned_by, writes_for ... 7 of the 40 are not in flo2.io's hub tool list (analyze_alternatives, apply_merge, certify_preservation, describe_designs, merge_designs, record_the_build, wall_check), so their flo2.io zero is no evidence. record_the_build is new since 0.91.0 and is the process tool for "record what was built": its steps were run by hand hundreds of times instead (add_change_event 737, set_artifact_checksums 391, add_verification 541).
D, a process step: 6. mint_seat (all 38 runs right before claim_region, none alone), satisfies (42 of 54 within two writes of add_capability, none alone), relation_candidates (70 of 80 next to review_relations, 1 alone), consumes and provides (14 of 17 and 16 of 18 next to each other, none alone), set_artifact_checksums (227 of 327 next to add_change_event, 207 right after it; 29 runs alone, so a step but not step-only).
THE SIX PAIRS NAMED IN THE INCREMENT: mint_seat then claim_region CONFIRMED; consumes and provides CONFIRMED; set_artifact_checksums after add_change_event CONFIRMED as a step, NOT step-only; satisfies after add_capability CONFIRMED; set_capability_status with replace_text REFUTED (38 of 88 runs, 43%; its neighbours spread over add_change_event 22, add_verification 17, set_artifact_checksums 17, which is record_the_build's process, not replace_text's); move_component REFUTED as a step (5 runs, never within two writes of contain_component or add_component; next to topic_report and propagate_from, a read then a move). One more found: relation_candidates then review_relations. None of the pairs occurs in the pilot or re-run logs, whose writers never called them.
E, close to another tool: 39, in the pairs the record already names (dec:idea-prune-the-tool-surface-to-an-orthogonal-essential-set kinds a to d) plus link_artifact/add_artifact, add_epoch/plan_epoch, scan_nodes/search_design. Clearest by counts: set_artifact_checksum 43 vs set_artifact_checksums 391 (mutual top-5 in the find_tools corpus); propagate_change 32 vs propagate_from 406; add_verification 541 vs verifies 49 (verifies is already its parameter); create_node 123 vs create_nodes 249; graph_report 23 vs graph_report_markdown 33; manual_work_ledger 2 vs report_manual_work 16; dimension_drift and dimension_drifts 0 and 0. The confusability replica on 0.95.0's toolsnaps: 58 mutual pairs, 25 tools not ranked first for their own job.
ALSO SEEN: mint_seat's reply names claim_region in a field that is not a cue field (`carry_it`), and it is the most-followed pointer in the sample (38 of 38), uncounted.
SAMPLE, honestly: a handful of agent sessions on two made-up projects, plus one month of flo2.io in which about 94% of calls are Anthony's, mostly his agents (fact:flo2-usage-baseline-2026-10-25 in the hub). Enough to see which cues are offered at the wrong moment and which pairs are run together; not enough to remove any tool (dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first).
